response_text:
Looking at this PR, I need to carefully analyze the changes to understand the impact on authentication flows.

Key observations:
1. `UsernameForm.java` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments
2. `UsernamePasswordForm.java` defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` with a required parameter
3. The `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` method requires `user != null`
4. The original code rendered webauthn form on fresh login (user null); the new code only does so when user is not null
5. Several existing/new tests rely on webauthn form being rendered on fresh login for conditional UI

      "line": 47,

      "title": "Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required argument",
      "body": "UsernameForm.authenticate() invokes isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm (line 160-162) requires a UserModel parameter. There is no no-arg overload in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. The change in UsernameForm.java is `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` — this will not compile. The fix is either to add a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() to UsernamePasswordForm (returning the realm passkeys-enabled state without requiring a user) or to pass context.getUser() into the existing method."
    },
    {

      "body": "The new helper isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requires user != null (line 161). In authenticate() it is now called unconditionally with context.getUser(), so when the user has not yet been identified (the fresh-login branch where context.getUser() == null), webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked. The previous code invoked fillContextForm inside the else branch when user was null and passkeys were enabled. As a result the conditional-UI challenge/RP ID/timeout/uv attributes are not populated on the initial login form, breaking discoverable-credential login and the existing tests PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (asserts webauth form is present on fresh login) and webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey (expects automatic login via discoverable key). The test webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication added in this PR also fails because its initial-login prerequisite depends on the same conditional UI."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java",
      "line": 137,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Regression: webauthn form no longer rendered on error when user is null",
      "body": "The overridden challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String error, String field) now guards fillContextForm behind isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which is false when context.getUser() is null. Previously the guard was `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` — i.e. fillContextForm ran on the user-not-found path. After the change, a USER_NOT_FOUND error during a fresh login no longer repopulates the webauthn form, so the conditional UI is broken on the error retry. This is a behavior reversal of the prior intent, not a fix."
    },

      "line": 161,
      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "isConditionalPasskeysEnabled parameter is dead — user != null check defeats the call sites",
      "body": "isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) is defined as `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. The `user != null` clause makes the parameter useless (the result does not depend on any user attribute — isPasskeysEnabled() is realm-level). All three callers (authenticate, error-challenge, and the broken UsernameForm call) would be more correct as a no-arg method that simply returns the realm passkeys state. The redundant `user != null` term is what causes the two regressions above. Either drop the parameter and the null check, or remove the `user != null` term so user=null still yields true when passkeys are realm-enabled."

findings.title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required argument
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() invokes isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition in the parent class UsernamePasswordForm (line 160-162) requires a UserModel parameter. There is no no-arg overload in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. The change in UsernameForm.java is `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())` — this will not compile. The fix is either to add a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() to UsernamePasswordForm (returning the realm passkeys-enabled state without requiring a user) or to pass context.getUser() into the existing method.

findings.title: Regression: webauthn conditional UI form no longer rendered on fresh login
findings.body: The new helper isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requires user != null (line 161). In authenticate() it is now called unconditionally with context.getUser(), so when the user has not yet been identified (the fresh-login branch where context.getUser() == null), webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked. The previous code invoked fillContextForm inside the else branch when user was null and passkeys were enabled. As a result the conditional-UI challenge/RP ID/timeout/uv attributes are not populated on the initial login form, breaking discoverable-credential login and the existing tests PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey (asserts webauth form is present on fresh login) and webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey (expects automatic login via discoverable key). The test webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication added in this PR also fails because its initial-login prerequisite depends on the same conditional UI.

findings.title: Regression: webauthn form no longer rendered on error when user is null
findings.body: The overridden challenge(AuthenticationFlowContext, String error, String field) now guards fillContextForm behind isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which is false when context.getUser() is null. Previously the guard was `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` — i.e. fillContextForm ran on the user-not-found path. After the change, a USER_NOT_FOUND error during a fresh login no longer repopulates the webauthn form, so the conditional UI is broken on the error retry. This is a behavior reversal of the prior intent, not a fix.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled parameter is dead — user != null check defeats the call sites
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) is defined as `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. The `user != null` clause makes the parameter useless (the result does not depend on any user attribute — isPasskeysEnabled() is realm-level). All three callers (authenticate, error-challenge, and the broken UsernameForm call) would be more correct as a no-arg method that simply returns the realm passkeys state. The redundant `user != null` term is what causes the two regressions above. Either drop the parameter and the null check, or remove the `user != null` term so user=null still yields true when passkeys are realm-enabled.
